raw.overview:
Pros
- Minimal investment and easy build requirements. 
- Excellent healing. 
- Good Stellar-Conduct DMG buffs. 
- Decent Cryo application after activating her Witch’s Revelation Passive. 
 Cons
- Reliance on Stellar-Conduct teammates for her strongest archetypes. 
- Lower Cryo application when the on-fielder plays outside of melee range. 
- Weak Constellations before C6. 
 Playstyles 
 Off-Field Support 
 Qiqi uses her Skill to provide healing and Cryo application. In Stellar-Conduct teams, she provides buffs that get even better at C6. She can also serve as a Cryo applier for some Forward Melt teams.
 On-Field DPS / Driver
 Qiqi can be a tanky driver for teammates’ coordinated attacks or serve as a Physical or Hybrid DPS. This playstyle is not covered in-depth in this Quick Guide.
 Talents 
 Level and Talent Priority
 Skill > Burst
 Qiqi’s buffs do not scale with Talent Levels and can be skipped entirely if her healing isn’t needed.
 Qiqi’s Elemental Skill is her main healing ability, so you should prioritize it if healing is needed. In Stellar-Conduct teams, her Burst can be leveled for damage; however, this is optional. Her Normal Attack Talent can also be left unleveled in most cases.
 Talent Overview
 Normal Attack
 Elemental Skill
 Elemental Burst
 Ascension 1 Passive
 Ascension 4 Passive
 Witch's Revelation Passive
 Normal Attack
 Normal Attack | Ancient Sword Art 
 Talent Description
 Normal Attack 
Performs up to 5 rapid strikes. 
 Charged Attack 
Consumes a certain amount Stamina to unleash 2 rapid sword strikes. 
 Plunging Attack 
Plunges from mid-air to strike the ground below, damaging opponents along the path and dealing AoE DMG upon impact. 
 Qiqi’s Normal Attacks are a fast 5-attack combo. Aside from driving her teammates’ abilities and triggering additional healing, Qiqi’s Normal Attacks don’t do much and can be left unleveled in a support playstyle.
 Elemental Skill
 Elemental Skill | Adeptus Art: Herald of Frost 
 Talent Description
 Using the Icevein Talisman, Qiqi brings forth the Herald of Frost, dealing Cryo DMG to surrounding opponents. 
 Herald of Frost 
On hit, Qiqi's Normal and Charged Attacks regenerate HP for your own party members and nearby teammates, with healing scaled based on Qiqi's ATK.
Periodically regenerates your active character's HP.
Follows the character around, dealing Cryo DMG to opponents in their path.
If your current active character hits an opponent with an attack, the Herald of Frost will perform a coordinated attack on the opponent, dealing Cryo DMG. 
 Qiqi’s Elemental Skill summons a Herald of Frost that orbits the active character, periodically deals Cryo damage, and heals the active character. While this Skill is active, Qiqi’s Normal Attacks that hit enemies heal the entire team; the healing scales with her ATK.
 After completing her “Witch’s Revelation” quest, this ability also generates Cryo particles and reduces her ER requirements. On top of that, the Herald of Frost also launches a coordinated attack (cooldown of 2.2s) when the active character hits an opponent. This is not limited to Normal or Charged Attacks; any ability triggers a coordinated attack. However, the ICD of the Cryo application is 2.5s/3 hits, which makes the Herald of Frost apply Cryo every other coordinated attack.
 Elemental Burst
 Elemental Burst | Adeptus Art: Preserver of Fortune 
 Talent Description
 Qiqi releases the adeptus power sealed within her body, marking nearby opponents with a Fortune-Preserving Talisman that deals Cryo DMG.
 Radiance: Stellar-Conduct: Deals an additional instance of Cryo DMG that is also considered Stellar-Conduct DMG. 
 Fortune-Preserving Talisman 
When opponents affected by this Talisman take DMG, the character that dealt this DMG regenerates HP. 
 Qiqi’s Elemental Burst deals a burst of AoE Cryo damage and marks each enemy it hits with a Fortune-Preserving Talisman. If an active character hits a marked enemy, that character is healed (scaling with Qiqi’s ATK).
 When inside the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, Qiqi’s Burst deals an additional hit of Stellar-Conduct DMG.
 Ascension 1 Passive
 Ascension 1 Passive | Life-Prolonging Methods 
 Talent Description
 When a character under the effects of Adeptus Art: Herald of Frost triggers an Elemental Reaction, their Incoming Healing Bonus is increased by 20% for 8s.
 Qiqi’s A1 Passive provides a bonus to incoming healing when the active character under the effects of Qiqi’s Elemental Skill triggers an Elemental Reaction. This is a welcomed boost to survivability, but Qiqi’s healing is already exceptional. Oftentimes, this passive isn’t noticeable.
 Ascension 4 Passive
 Ascension 4 Passive | A Glimpse Into Arcanum 
 Talent Description
 When Qiqi hits opponents with her Normal and Charged Attacks, she has a 50% chance to apply a Fortune-Preserving Talisman to them for 6s. This effect can only occur once every 30s.
 Radiance: Stellar-Conduct: The effect now has a 100% chance to trigger, and cooldown time is reduced to 15s. 
 With her A4 Passive, Qiqi’s Normal Attacks have a 50% chance to mark an enemy with a Fortune-Preserving Talisman, like the ones from her Burst, for 6s once every 30s. This is also a nice buff to her healing but has quite some downtime. However, when in the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, it has a 100% chance to trigger and the cooldown is reduced to 15s, which fixes the downtime issue.
 Witch's Revelation Passive
 Witch's Revelation Passive | Seven Sacred Treasures 
 Talent Description
 The cooldown of the Elemental Skill Adeptus Art: Herald of Frost is reduced to 15s.
 Radiance: Stellar-Conduct: While the Herald of Frost is on the field, characters in Qiqi's party have their Superconduct and Stellar-Conduct Reaction DMG increased by 50%.
Additionally, when inside a Polestar Field, Qiqi will enter the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state. 
 Qiqi’s Witch’s Revelation Passive is her most important passive. After completing her “Witch’s Revelation” quest, Qiqi’s Elemental Skill cooldown reduces to 15s, which gives her full uptime on her Skill. Qiqi also enters the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state when she is inside a Polestar Field. When she is in this state, she gives a teamwide Superconduct and Stellar-Conduct buff.
 Constellations 
 Constellation 1

 Constellation 1
 Constellation 1 | Ascetics of Frost 
 Constellation Description
 Qiqi regenerates 2 Energy when the Herald of Frost hits an opponent marked by a Fortune-Preserving Talisman.
 Radiance: Stellar-Conduct: Qiqi also regenerates 6 Elemental Energy when the Herald of Frost's attacks and coordinated attacks hit opponents. This effect can trigger once every 6s. 
 This Constellation gives Qiqi 2 Energy when her Skill hits an opponent marked with a Fortune-Preserving Talisman. Additionally, when in the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, she gets an additional 6 Energy with a 6s cooldown. This helps reduce her ER requirements.

 Constellation 2 | Frozen to the Bone 
 Constellation Description
 Qiqi's Normal and Charge Attack DMG against opponents affected by Cryo is increased by 15%.
 Radiance: Stellar-Conduct: Qiqi's ATK is increased by 50%. 
 Qiqi’s C2 grants a small DMG% buff to her Normal and Charged Attacks in teams with good Cryo aura uptime. In the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, she also gains a nice 50% ATK buff, which improves her healing and her C6 Stellar-Conduct buffs.

 Constellation 4
 Constellation 4 | Divine Suppression 
 Constellation Description
 Targets marked by a Fortune-Preserving Talisman have their ATK reduced by 20%.
Additionally, when the healing effect of Fortune-Preserving Talisman triggers, the nearby party member with the lowest HP percentage remaining will also receive an additional instance of healing for 180% of Qiqi's ATK. 
 Qiqi’s C4 is one of the few sources of enemy ATK Reduction in the game. With her Witch’s Revelation Passive, her lowest–HP percentage teammate also receives additional healing. This passive can be useful if you keep getting hit by powerful enemies.
 Constellation 5
 Constellation 5 | Crimson Lotus Bloom 
 Constellation Description
 Increases the Level of Adeptus Art: Herald of Frost by 3.
Maximum upgrade level is 15. 
 A straightforward +3 level increase to her Skill.
 Constellation 6
 Constellation 6 | Rite of Resurrection 
 Constellation Description
 Using Adeptus Art: Preserver of Fortune revives all fallen party members nearby and regenerates 50% of their HP.
This effect can only occur once every 15 mins.
Additionally, after using Adeptus Art: Preserver of Fortune, Qiqi will also gain 4 stacks of Glimpse of Mystery, and when your current active character (other than Qiqi) deals Stellar-Conduct DMG, 1 stack of Glimpse of Mystery is consumed, and DMG dealt is increased by 600% of Qiqi's ATK. The Glimpse of Mystery effect lasts up to 12s, and unleashing Adeptus Art: Preserver of Fortune refreshes the stack count. 
 Qiqi’s C6 is her best Constellation.
 This ability revives all fallen teammates on a 15-minute cooldown.
 After completing Qiqi’s “Witch’s Revelation” quest, this Constellation also introduces a big buff, called Glimpse of Misery, to Stellar-Conduct damage that scales with her ATK. Qiqi’s Glimpse of Misery functions similarly to Illuga's Nightingale Song.
 This Constellation makes 4pc Noblesse Oblige a worthwhile alternative to 4pc Tenacity of the Millelith because Qiqi should now use her Burst every rotation. It also incentivizes Qiqi to equip Swords with an ATK% secondary stat like Finale of the Deep over other options like Favonius Sword.
raw.erRequirements:
In Stellar-Conduct teams where Qiqi is at C6, it is optimal to use her Burst every rotation. In most other teams and before Qiqi is C6, she does not have to use her Burst. Qiqi’s healing from her Skill and A4 Passive is already enough for survivability in most cases. As such, Qiqi can forgo ER investment entirely and use her Burst every other rotation, when available, or when needed.
 Assumptions:
- Safe particle RNG and default enemy particles are assumed. 
- Relevant teammates other than Qiqi hold Favonius Weapons where applicable. 
- When Qiqi holds Favonius Sword, her ER requirements decrease by 20–30%. 
 Qiqi’s C1 lowers her ER requirements significantly, especially in Stellar-Conduct teams. The exact Energy refund depends on whether the Herald of Frost can hit the enemy consistently. The table below assumes consistent hits in the Melee column and doesn’t in the Ranged column.
 C0 C1 + Melee C1 + Ranged 
 With Sandrone 240–285% 150–170% 190–220% 
 With Sandrone + 1 Cryo 220–245% 135–155% 170–190% 
 Use the Energy Recharge Calculator to determine exact requirements for your team and rotation. For more details on how Favonius weapons will affect your team, please use Ac1d’s Favonius Mastersheet .

 ATK% ATK% CRIT Rate (Fav.) or ATK% or Healing Bonus 
 Stat Priority: ER until requirement > ATK% > CRIT Rate (Favonius) > Flat ATK
 Qiqi’s healing and C6 buff scale with ATK. With Favonius Sword, a CRIT Rate Circlet helps trigger Favonius Sword’s passive more consistently. At C6, an ATK% Circlet can be best since her Stellar-Conduct buffs scale with ATK.
 A Healing Bonus Circlet can increase Qiqi’s healing even further, but this is generally unnecessary.
raw.artifactSets:
Hover over artifact images for more information. 
 4pc Tenacity of the Millelith (TotM) 4pc TotM is a good buffing set with ATK-scaling teammates. However, if Qiqi is C6 in Stellar-Conduct teams, 4pc Noblesse Oblige may be preferred to let another teammate hold 4pc TotM instead. 
 4pc Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City (Scroll) 4pc Scroll gives a teamwide 12% DMG Bonus to the Element with which Qiqi triggers a reaction. In teams without an ATK-scaling DPS or where 4pc TotM is already in use, this set can be a decent alternative.
If Qiqi is on a team with a Natlan teammate, they may be better suited to hold this set instead since they can activate the set’s full Elemental DMG Bonus. 
 4pc Instructor 4pc Instructor grants the team 120 EM for 8s if Qiqi triggers an Elemental Reaction while on-field. 
 4pc Noblesse Oblige (NO) 4pc NO is a good alternative to 4pc TotM in teams where Qiqi uses her Burst every rotation. However, this may extend the rotation or lead to unfeasible ER requirements in most teams, making 4pc NO undesirable.
However, if Qiqi is C6 in a Stellar-Conduct team, she may hold this set to let another teammate hold 4pc TotM instead. 
 4pc Ocean-Hued Clam (OHC) 4pc OHC is an option in teams where Qiqi has more field time. Qiqi can easily max out the upper limit of the Sea-Dyed Foam’s healing absorption to deal 27,000 AoE Physical damage every 3.5s. In teams with an Electro character, the damage from the Sea-Dyed Foam increases thanks to Superconduct’s Physical RES Shred.
In off-field teams, this set can still work but a lot of teams prefer more supportive options that buff Qiqi’s teammates directly 
 4pc Song of Days Past (SoDP) 4pc SoDP is another buffing set that records the amount of healing done and converts it into an Additive DMG Bonus. However, the buffs from this set may be used up fast in multi-target combat or by the wrong teammate.
raw.weapons:
Hover over weapon images/names for more information. 
 Favonius Sword Favonius Sword is the best option for decreasing both Qiqi’s and her teammates’ ER requirements. Qiqi requires some CRIT Rate investment to consistently trigger Favonius’s passive. 
 Freedom-Sworn Freedom-Sworn’s passive gives a teamwide Normal Attack, Charged Attack, and Plunging Attack DMG Bonus and ATK%. Qiqi needs to trigger two reactions to proc this passive, which may be difficult in some teams. 
 Key of Khaj-Nisut Key of Khaj-Nisut provides a large teamwide EM buff, which can make it a strong option for team damage in Melt teams. Qiqi can build HP% main stats to increase the passive at the cost of her healing output. 
 Peak Patrol Song Peak Patrol Song gives an Elemental DMG% buff based on the wearer’s DEF. This can be an option for teams that deal a lot of Elemental damage. Qiqi should build some DEF (up to 3200) to maximize the passive, which is easier thanks to her high Base DEF. Make sure Qiqi performs at least 2 Normal Attacks to activate this weapon’s passive. 
 Finale of the Deep Finale of the Deep is a craftable weapon from Fontaine. It offers the most ATK% for a 4-star weapon. Qiqi can easily trigger the first part of its passive.
At R5, assuming Qiqi can fully clear the Bond of Life, this option grants more ATK than any other Sword on the list, aside from refined 5-star options. 
 Azurelight ⓘ , Summit Shaper ⓘ , Aquila Favonia ⓘ These 5-star weapons have high total ATK. But, they are only worth using if you have them available and do not want to waste billets crafting Finale of the Deep. 
 Other ATK% Swords If you have no billets for Finale of the Deep, other ATK% Swords can be used. However, Finale of the Deep is generally a better weapon. 
 Xiphos Moonlight Xiphos’ Moonlight gives ER% to the entire team based on Qiqi’s EM. Qiqi should build EM main stats to maximize this passive. However, Favonius Sword is generally a better choice. 
 Sacrificial Sword Sacrificial Sword is no longer needed for full uptime on Qiqi’s Skill, thanks to her Witch’s Revelation Passive.
raw.teams:
Rotation Notation
- N = Normal Attack 
- C = Charged Attack 
- A = Aimed Shot 
- P = Plunging Attack 
- E = Elemental Skill 
- tE = Tap Skill 
- hE = Hold Skill 
- Q = Elemental Burst 
- D = dash (cancel) 
- J = jump (cancel) 
- W = walk (cancel) 
- > = switch character 
- ( ) = these actions are optional; please refer to the notes below 
- [ ] = repeat these actions the specified number of times 
 Stellar-Conduct 
 Qiqi — Sandrone — Electro — Flex 
 Qiqi is one of Sandrone’s best teammates in Stellar-Conduct. Her Cryo application, buffs, and particle generation make her one of the core teammates in this archetype.
 Notable Teammates
 Sandrone ★ As a Stellar-Conduct DPS, Sandrone appreciates Qiqi’s buffs and particle generation. 
 Off-field Electro
 An off-field Electro applier is mandatory to trigger Stellar-Conduct in teams with Sandrone.
 Yae Miko ★ Yae Miko is the preferred Electro option for Stellar-Conduct. She benefits from Qiqi’s buffs as she deals Stellar-Conduct DMG herself. 
 C6 Beidou At C6, Beidou is the preferred replacement for Yae Miko. After completing her Witch’s Revelation quest, she provides valuable Cryo RES Shred and an EM buff to the on-fielder.
She is also available from the Starglitter Exchange and Lantern Rite events, making it easier to gain her Constellations. 
 Kuki Shinobu 
 Fischl 
 Flex
 These characters provide buffs or damage.
 Nicole ★ Nicole provides an ATK% buff to the whole team and a shield, which the team appreciates. The Arcane Projections produced by her Burst do not interfere with any Elemental Reactions; however, Nicole generally does not Burst in Stellar-Conduct teams to reduce the team’s rotation length.
Nicole uses 2pc ATK% + 2pc ATK% in Stellar-Conduct teams. 
 C6 Diona At C6, Diona provides an EM buff and a Stellar-Conduct DMG buff to the active character in her Burst’s AoE.
While in a Polestar Field generated by the Stellar-Conduct reaction, her Skill provides additional off-field Cryo application and allows her to hold 4pc TotM. 
 Escoffier Escoffier’s Cryo RES Shred, particle generation, and personal damage make her a viable option for Stellar-Conduct by lack of other options.
However, Escoffier will not have her maximum amount of RES Shred since the team does not consist solely of Hydro and Cryo teammates. Additionally, Electro teammates like Yae Miko cannot benefit from her RES Shred since the Stellar-Conduct damage they deal is considered Electro DMG. 
 Cyno Cyno can be played as an on-field or quickswap DPS in Stellar Conduct teams where he appreciates Qiqi’s buffs and Cryo application. However, he competes with Sandrone for field time and has limited synergy with her. It seems that his Stellar-Conduct teams will have to wait for future characters to be released. 
 Wriothesley Wriothesley has anti-synergy with Qiqi, as her healing can lower the amount of special Charged Attacks he can perform. Considering her Burst increases Qiqi’s healing output even further, her C6 buff can also be harder to use.
Qiqi can still work with Wriothesley for her Stellar-Conduct buff, but she should use gear that minimizes her healing output (e.g. unleveled artifact pieces). 
 Xilonen 
 Sucrose 
 Zhongli 
 Iansan 
 Bennett 
 4pc VV Anemo Supports 
 Example Teams
 This is not a comprehensive list of teams. The inclusion or exclusion of any given team does not necessarily reflect its power level.
 Qiqi — Sandrone — Yae Miko — Nicole / Escoffier 
 A strong Sandrone team with Yae Miko and Nicole or Escoffier. Nicole provides an ATK% buff to Sandrone and Yae, while Escoffier provides Cryo particles, minor Cryo RES Shred, and some personal damage.
 Sample Rotation (Nicole) 
Yae 3[E] > Qiqi E (Q)¹ > Nicole E > Sandrone combo
 Sample Rotation (Escoffier) 
Yae 3[E] > Escoffier E > Qiqi E (Q)¹ > Sandrone combo
¹If Qiqi is C6.
 Qiqi — Sandrone — C6 Beidou — C6 Diona 
 This Sandrone team particularly shines with Beidou’s and Diona’s C6. Beidou’s and Diona’s shields, on top of Qiqi’s and Diona’s heals, make this team very comfortable to play.
 Sample Rotation 
Qiqi E (Q)¹ > Beidou EQ > Diona hEQ > Sandrone combo
¹If Qiqi is C6.
 General Support 
 Qiqi — Flex — Flex — Flex 
 Qiqi’s healing and Cryo application can work for many teams.
 Notable Teammates
 Cryo
 Qiqi can work with other Cryo characters in Freeze teams or serve as a secondary Cryo applier in Forward Melt teams. Qiqi can also help battery other Cryo units and provide healing.
 Citlali Qiqi can serve as secondary Cryo application alongside Citlali in Forward Melt teams with a Pyro DPS, supplementing her Cryo to allow for more lenient Melt timings or additional Melted hits. In Freeze teams, Citlali shreds Hydro RES and holds 4pc Scroll while Qiqi can act as a sustain. 
 Skirk 
 Ayaka 
 Wriothesley 
 Eula 
 Freminet 
 Rosaria 
 Kaeya 
 Hydro
 Qiqi can provide Frozen uptime in teams with Hydro characters.
 Furina Qiqi provides healing to offset Furina’s HP drain and stack Fanfare. 
 Neuvillette 
 Ayato 
 Tartaglia 
 Yelan 
 Xingqiu 
 Mona 
 Pyro
 Mavuika / Arlecchino Qiqi’s Skill provides enough Cryo application for Pyro DPS units like Mavuika and Arlecchino to Melt their hits. Melee DPS units are preferred, as her Cryo application comes from both the Herald of Frost and the coordinated attacks. As such, ranged DPS units like Yoimiya and Lyney require an additional Cryo applier on the team. 
 Durin 
 Gaming 
 Dehya 
 Diluc 
 Other
 For certain non-PHEC DPS units, Qiqi provides Cryo application and healing.
 Chasca 
 Navia 
 Varka 
 Example Teams
 This is not a comprehensive list of teams. The inclusion or exclusion of any given team does not necessarily reflect its power level.
 Qiqi — Skirk — Furina — Shenhe / Mona 
 Qiqi acts as a defensive Cryo option for Skirk, provides healing for Fanfare, and generates particles for the team. Qiqi can hold 4pc Scroll if Furina holds 4pc TotM.
 Sample Rotation (Mona) 
Furina ED Q > Qiqi N1 E (Q)¹ > Mona EQ > Skirk combo
 Sample Rotation (Shenhe) 
Furina ED Q > Qiqi N1 E (Q)¹ > Shenhe hEQ > Skirk combo
¹Use Burst when available.
 Qiqi — Arlecchino — Bennett — Sucrose 
 Sucrose must deplete the Pyro aura from Bennett’s Burst prior to Arlecchino taking the field.
 If possible, cancel Arlecchino’s Charged Attack to get more reliable Melts.
 Sample Rotation 
Arlecchino E > Bennett EQ > Qiqi E > Sucrose N1 E > Arlecchino C¹ 6[N3D]
¹Dash cancel this Charged Attack for more reliable Melts. Alternatively, you can wait for the Cryo aura to be reapplied before starting the Normal Attacks.
 Qiqi — Eula — Furina — Raiden / Rosaria 
 Now that Qiqi generates particles on her Skill, she can be a Cryo battery for Eula. With her ability to generate Fanfare for Furina, she’s a decent pick in this team.
 Raiden provides Superconduct uptime, Energy regeneration, and personal damage. Rosaria is a more accessible unit who can be a second Cryo battery and provides a modest CRIT Rate buff. At C6, Rosaria also shreds Physical RES.

²Use Burst when available.

 A tried and trusted staple. Qiqi uses Normal Attacks to drive the coordinated attacks from herself, Xingqiu, Beidou, and C6 Fischl.
 Make sure to alternate between Fischl’s Burst and Skill between rotations to ensure optimal uptime for Oz. Qiqi’s Cryo application enables Superconduct, which benefits 4pc Ocean-Hued Clam’s damage. 4pc TotM is still an option as it buffs the entire team.

raw.playstyles:
Off-Field Support 
 Qiqi uses her Skill to provide healing and Cryo application. In Stellar-Conduct teams, she provides buffs that get even better at C6. She can also serve as a Cryo applier for some Forward Melt teams.
 On-Field DPS / Driver
 Qiqi can be a tanky driver for teammates’ coordinated attacks or serve as a Physical or Hybrid DPS. This playstyle is not covered in-depth in this Quick Guide.
raw.stellarConduct:
Qiqi — Sandrone — Electro — Flex 
 Qiqi is one of Sandrone’s best teammates in Stellar-Conduct. Her Cryo application, buffs, and particle generation make her one of the core teammates in this archetype.
 Notable Teammates
 Sandrone ★ As a Stellar-Conduct DPS, Sandrone appreciates Qiqi’s buffs and particle generation. 
 Off-field Electro
 An off-field Electro applier is mandatory to trigger Stellar-Conduct in teams with Sandrone.
 Yae Miko ★ Yae Miko is the preferred Electro option for Stellar-Conduct. She benefits from Qiqi’s buffs as she deals Stellar-Conduct DMG herself. 
 C6 Beidou At C6, Beidou is the preferred replacement for Yae Miko. After completing her Witch’s Revelation quest, she provides valuable Cryo RES Shred and an EM buff to the on-fielder.
She is also available from the Starglitter Exchange and Lantern Rite events, making it easier to gain her Constellations. 
 Kuki Shinobu 
 Fischl 
 Flex
 These characters provide buffs or damage.
 Nicole ★ Nicole provides an ATK% buff to the whole team and a shield, which the team appreciates. The Arcane Projections produced by her Burst do not interfere with any Elemental Reactions; however, Nicole generally does not Burst in Stellar-Conduct teams to reduce the team’s rotation length.
Nicole uses 2pc ATK% + 2pc ATK% in Stellar-Conduct teams. 
 C6 Diona At C6, Diona provides an EM buff and a Stellar-Conduct DMG buff to the active character in her Burst’s AoE.
While in a Polestar Field generated by the Stellar-Conduct reaction, her Skill provides additional off-field Cryo application and allows her to hold 4pc TotM. 
 Escoffier Escoffier’s Cryo RES Shred, particle generation, and personal damage make her a viable option for Stellar-Conduct by lack of other options.
However, Escoffier will not have her maximum amount of RES Shred since the team does not consist solely of Hydro and Cryo teammates. Additionally, Electro teammates like Yae Miko cannot benefit from her RES Shred since the Stellar-Conduct damage they deal is considered Electro DMG. 
 Cyno Cyno can be played as an on-field or quickswap DPS in Stellar Conduct teams where he appreciates Qiqi’s buffs and Cryo application. However, he competes with Sandrone for field time and has limited synergy with her. It seems that his Stellar-Conduct teams will have to wait for future characters to be released. 
 Wriothesley Wriothesley has anti-synergy with Qiqi, as her healing can lower the amount of special Charged Attacks he can perform. Considering her Burst increases Qiqi’s healing output even further, her C6 buff can also be harder to use.
Qiqi can still work with Wriothesley for her Stellar-Conduct buff, but she should use gear that minimizes her healing output (e.g. unleveled artifact pieces).

sets.name: Tenacity of the Millelith
sets.note: 4pc TotM is a good buffing set with ATK-scaling teammates. However, if Qiqi is C6 in Stellar-Conduct teams, 4pc Noblesse Oblige may be preferred to let another teammate hold 4pc TotM instead.

sets.name: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
sets.note: 4pc Scroll gives a teamwide 12% DMG Bonus to the Element with which Qiqi triggers a reaction. In teams without an ATK-scaling DPS or where 4pc TotM is already in use, this set can be a decent alternative. If Qiqi is on a team with a Natlan teammate, they may be better suited to hold this set instead since they can activate the set’s full Elemental DMG Bonus.

sets.name: Instructor
sets.note: 4pc Instructor grants the team 120 EM for 8s if Qiqi triggers an Elemental Reaction while on-field.

sets.name: Noblesse Oblige
sets.note: 4pc NO is a good alternative to 4pc TotM in teams where Qiqi uses her Burst every rotation. However, this may extend the rotation or lead to unfeasible ER requirements in most teams, making 4pc NO undesirable. However, if Qiqi is C6 in a Stellar-Conduct team, she may hold this set to let another teammate hold 4pc TotM instead.

sets.name: Ocean-Hued Clam
sets.note: 4pc OHC is an option in teams where Qiqi has more field time. Qiqi can easily max out the upper limit of the Sea-Dyed Foam’s healing absorption to deal 27,000 AoE Physical damage every 3.5s. In teams with an Electro character, the damage from the Sea-Dyed Foam increases thanks to Superconduct’s Physical RES Shred. In off-field teams, this set can still work but a lot of teams prefer more supportive options that buff Qiqi’s teammates directly

sets.name: Song of Days Past
sets.note: 4pc SoDP is another buffing set that records the amount of healing done and converts it into an Additive DMG Bonus. However, the buffs from this set may be used up fast in multi-target combat or by the wrong teammate.

constellations.1: Ascetics of Frost Qiqi regenerates 2 Energy when the Herald of Frost hits an opponent marked by a Fortune-Preserving Talisman. Radiance: Stellar-Conduct: Qiqi also regenerates 6 Elemental Energy when the Herald of Frost's attacks and coordinated attacks hit opponents. This effect can trigger once every 6s. This Constellation gives Qiqi 2 Energy when her Skill hits an opponent marked with a Fortune-Preserving Talisman. Additionally, when in the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, she gets an additional 6 Energy with a 6s cooldown. This helps reduce her ER requirements. Constellation 2
constellations.2: Frozen to the Bone Qiqi's Normal and Charge Attack DMG against opponents affected by Cryo is increased by 15%. Radiance: Stellar-Conduct: Qiqi's ATK is increased by 50%. Qiqi’s C2 grants a small DMG% buff to her Normal and Charged Attacks in teams with good Cryo aura uptime. In the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, she also gains a nice 50% ATK buff, which improves her healing and her C6 Stellar-Conduct buffs. Constellation 3
constellations.3: Ascendant Praise Increases the Level of Adeptus Art: Preserver of Fortune by 3. Maximum upgrade level is 15. A simple +3 level increase to her Burst. Constellation 4
constellations.4: Divine Suppression Targets marked by a Fortune-Preserving Talisman have their ATK reduced by 20%. Additionally, when the healing effect of Fortune-Preserving Talisman triggers, the nearby party member with the lowest HP percentage remaining will also receive an additional instance of healing for 180% of Qiqi's ATK. Qiqi’s C4 is one of the few sources of enemy ATK Reduction in the game. With her Witch’s Revelation Passive, her lowest–HP percentage teammate also receives additional healing. This passive can be useful if you keep getting hit by powerful enemies. Constellation 5
